title: Stored x-only leaf birthday search on secp256k1 at 125.211359085293: six leaves per batched inverse, a fraction class key read from x for a third of leaves, metered rare-carry branches and a paired range scan

claims.statement: For uniform production secp256k1 Q=[x]P, the classical cold stored-leaf birthday search of proof.md recovers x with probability at least 0.390000001 over the challenge and fresh algorithm coins, with no heuristic: the Chen-Stein method on cross-node leaf pairs bounds P(no collision), and drops, caps, wrong class indices and the enumerated carry sites of the kernels (section 3.4) are charged failure rows, as are the caps of two meters, while RNDR, the ideal coin source, adds none (section 6). On every run its total work is at most 2^125.211359085293 target-group-operation equivalents (1000 AArch64 instructions per unit). Each pair of generator points X, Y gives six leaves, the x-coordinates of phi^t(X) + Y and phi^t(X) - Y for t = 0, 1, 2, from one batched inverse of y_Y^2 - y_X^2 (section 3.1). A leaf's key is the top 176 bits of its class's canonical x-coordinate v* = min(x, beta x, beta^2 x): a leaf of class index j = 0 reads it from x with no arithmetic, and j = 1 and j = 2 extend KEY's top column of x*beta/p by two columns of a truncated product with floor(beta*2^448/p) (j = 2 then subtracts from x). The path values are proved to lie within 7 below and 10 above floor(2^192 v*/p), so a window test on their low 16 bits drops every leaf near a boundary (a charged row below 2^-9.6 per leaf) and every other leaf whose index is exact emits exactly v* >> 80 (section 3.3); a weighted meter counts the two paths' instructions. KEY's index needs no windows: a wrong index, on a set of rate below 2^-54.29, is a charged missed collision, and classes sharing the 176 bits give false candidates charged through the mass bound KB(f) = 6*2^(256-f)(1 + 2^-13)/(r-1). Machine (section 2.1): 2^72 nodes, each with one processor (base AArch64 with FEAT_RNG and FEAT_LSE) and a memory below 2^64 bytes, whose links deliver a message's four words at the address its sender stored and keep no flags, rings or counters. Beyond its sender's instructions, every message's charge includes 8 instruction-equivalents at each hop: its delivery as route.s dlv (6), which the experiment executes for every message of its 4 x 4 run, and its port's in-flight count (2). Hop 1, hop 2 and grouping are charged 19, 18.25 and 17.546875 per record; the grouping's scan_ranges compares K2 only, within each d4 range, in CMP/CCMP pairs at 195/64 per record plus at most 26 per range and 8 per candidate, and its matches of different classes on the 176 key bits are charged to the candidate, request and relay caps (2^28, 2^29, 2^34; section 6.4). The rare carries and borrows of the field macros (SHX, FDX, F5, FS, FADDW) are taken by a branch over a fixup that completes the chain, so every result is bit-identical to an inline chain; a fixup costs 3 or 4 instructions and is counted, and a node starts a batch only while its fixups are at most 2^45 - 46 q2, so the ledger charges 4*2^45 per node and Markov's inequality on the fixups' mean (below 2^28.35 per node, from the operand sets of section 3.4) charges the cap (section 3.4). certificate.py gives at most 355.7798 instructions per leaf and the claim 125.211359085293. Peak memory at most 2^135.9988 bytes; preprocessing at most 2^110.2061 units, included; no advice; certificate.py checks that the work, memory and preprocessing figures are the least 12-decimal (work) or 4-decimal (memory, preprocessing) values at or above their exact values, and that 0.390000001 is below the success bound. The bound is for the machine of section 2.1. Lineage: our 5b6cd013 (the base package: metered rare-carry branches on the windowless KEY and range-local scan of our 502d7155 and eb0aea59), f9d5a673 (transport and grouping) and b3716a20 (the six-leaf fwd and bwd kernels, the site table and the success argument), package 8f733826 (field rows and FS) with c8a6819e (kernel macros, a64.py), 02feb284 (fe_inv, the F0 and F1 rows), 4595bad7 (SB6's stored-offset subtraction) and fce6e7ef (link-side counter updates charged), submissions 3828873f, 6ef3e7b3, d637fb0a, 9798f5f4 and d9e3dbf4 (STADD, paired scan comparisons, prefix4, the generator and candidate allowances, a claim on a decimal grid), 472226d8, 4fdb8a9c and e1ecd7cc (a success target nearer 0.39, a 12-decimal claim), 80e9e8af and 1efcef88 (the range-local scan), 892a3df8 and b00400fa (its paired 64-record form, taken unchanged), 1fbd26e8 (the candidate charge at twice its itemized work), and 807e4bf5 and a9297fb0 (rare exits to charged stubs and a per-walk meter); new here are the fraction key (j = 0 read from x, the truncated extension for j = 1 and 2 with proven error bounds and windows, the drop and mass bounds, the weighted key-path meter) and its 176-bit record layout; no prior acceptance or score is a premise. This is an analytic bound, not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Run the six-leaf kernels on production points, with every emitted key of a leaf outside KEY's window set against the top 176 bits of its class's canonical x and the class-key test on random and window-edge classes, and the emit, both hops (each message delivered by executing dlv) and the grouping (with the paired scan_ranges) on a 4 x 4 machine, against exact references; check the arithmetic sites and rare-carry fixups of section 3.4 (sites.py; planted points force fixups in both passes, planted leaves force window drops), including both key paths; compare the counts of the leaf, inversion, transport, delivery and grouping kernels with certificate.py; run the q25 toy (toy.py) with six leaves per incidence and certificate.py. Budget-limited parts run stated minimums. Not a production-scale attack.
